ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: High contrast ratio characterized by a dominant low-intensity (dark charcoal) base with approximately 15-20% high-intensity (white/light grey) pixel clusters distributed as localized spots.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: High density of discrete, small-scale white annular and circular blobs (mottling) distributed across the entire visible ventral surface, with increased frequency of contiguous white pixels towards the lateral tips and trailing edges.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Shallow, wide U-shaped depression; central vertex is partially obscured by water line but suggests an obtuse angle of approximately 130-145 degrees.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Continuous high-frequency serration pattern along the trailing edge of both lobes; characterized by irregular peaks and valleys with a pixel amplitude of 5-15 pixels relative to the mean edge line.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Convex curve extending from the median notch to the distal tips, terminating in sharp, slightly upward-curving lateral points.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Extensive spatial detection of circular high-contrast pixel clusters (annular rings) consistent with sessile organism attachment scars, covering >40% of the visible surface area.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Several distinct, unaligned linear pixel disruptions (white scratches) are visible, notably a long diagonal mark on the right lobe and multiple vertical rake-like marks on the left lobe.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Live sessile barnacle colonies (white, high-relief clusters) are visible protruding from the far lateral tips of both the left and right fluke lobes.
other_distinctive_markers: The extreme accumulation of barnacles at the tips creates an irregular, jagged distal silhouette that is distinct from the natural serration of the fluke edge.
